structure: 26 lines, zero bloat, every rule load-bearing; lean enough that a references/ split is unnecessary

actionability: numbered rules with exit codes and stderr contract documented ('Exit codes: 0 success, 1 the document could not be converted, 2 usage error, 3 pages of a PDF need OCR... Failures print one anydoc: <message> line to stderr' — lint's error_handling warn is wrong), dep check ('It needs Node 20+'), and context-hygiene guidance ('write to a file with -o and read the parts you need')

safety: keep lint 4 — secret_proximity hit reviewed and cleared ('Pass --api-key or set FIRECRAWL_API_KEY' are parameter names, not secrets), but the documented fallback sends document contents to a third party ('Rerun with --ocr hosted to send it to Firecrawl Parse') with no ask-user-first instruction, and 'npx -y @firecrawl/anydoc' fetches an unpinned package from npm at runtime
portability: standard frontmatter (name/description/license/metadata.author), Node 20+ requirement, no absolute or platform-locked paths
